name: Palace Jailer
oracle_text:
When this creature enters, you become the monarch.
When this creature enters, exile target creature an opponent controls until an opponent becomes the monarch.
blocked_sentences: When this creature enters, you become the monarch.
When this creature enters, exile target creature an opponent controls until an opponent becomes the monarch.

needs.what: An exile whose return is keyed to a future *event* and whose lifetime is independent of the permanent that exiled it: `exile` needs an `until` duration alongside its existing `until_leaves`, taking an event (here `becomes_monarch` filtered to an opponent of the exiling controller) and returning the linked card to the battlefield under its owner's control when that event first occurs -- once, then the link is discharged. Crucially the return must survive the exiling permanent leaving the battlefield, and must never happen merely *because* it left.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `exile` with `until_leaves` is the only duration it has, and `ops_board.py:101-104` documents it as the O-Ring family: it records `obj.exiled_by = ctx.source_oid` and nothing else, and the return is a separate ordinary `leaves_battlefield` triggered ability on the same card reading `{"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"}`. That is wrong for Palace Jailer twice over, in opposite directions: it returns the creature on an event that must *not* return it (Palace Jailer dying leaves the creature exiled indefinitely -- the exile is a one-shot effect with a duration, not an effect the permanent maintains), and it cannot return it on the event that must (nothing links a `leaves_battlefield` trigger to a monarchy change). Writing it as `until_leaves` would hand the opponent their creature back for the price of killing a 2/2, which is a materially different and much weaker card. The `delay` op is the only mechanism in `ops` that outlives its source -- `ops_control.py:376-399` captures bindings now and fires later with no object to hang a trigger on, which is exactly the right *lifetime* -- but `DelayedTrigger` is keyed on `step` (a phase name, defaulting to `end_step`) and has no event slot, so it can schedule "at the beginning of the next end step" and cannot schedule "the next time an opponent becomes the monarch". Giving `DelayedTrigger` an optional event condition is the likely shape of this work, and would also serve the wider "exile until <event>" family.

closest_existing: exile with until_leaves plus a leaves_battlefield trigger reading exiled_with: self (O-Ring, Fiend Hunter)
rest_is_expressible: Everything that is not the monarch loads already. The body is a plain 2/2 Human Soldier for {2}{W}{W} with no keywords, and both abilities are `self_enters` triggers. The second ability's target -- "target creature an opponent controls" -- is an ordinary target spec (`types: ["Creature"]`, `controller: "opponent"`), and the exile itself is the existing `exile` op with `objects: {"target": ...}`. Only the monarch designation and the exile's duration are missing. No partial answer was written: an answer could only have been either a 2/2 that exiles a creature permanently (dropping the printed duration outright) or one that returns it when the Jailer dies (`until_leaves`), and both are the substituted-nearby-op failure the brief forbids -- the duration is the whole reason this card is a four-mana 2/2 rather than a strictly better Journey to Nowhere. Dropping only the first line is not available either, since "you become the monarch" is what makes the second line's duration reachable at all.
resolved_note: `monarch` shipped: `GameState.monarch`, the two inherent triggered abilities of rule 721.3 (the end-step draw and the combat-damage transfer), the `become_monarch` op with a player selector, the `is_monarch` and `no_monarch` condition keys and the `becomes_monarch` trigger event. The needs listed here are what is still missing.
